The FBI didn't do a lot of the background check for DoD DSS. They did some as time premitted, but mostly the DSS use contractors to do background checks.

The way the process worked is a request for clearance came to DSS. It was assigned a case number and assigned to a case manager. The case manager checked over the background information and locations the person lived. Most people lived (because the US is a mobile population) in multiple locations around the country. Therefore the case manager would sent out background check request to multiple FBI field offices or contract investigators. It often took over a year to get all the checks completed at it was handled as 'other duties as assigned' by the FBI field offices and the various military investigative agencies. DSS operated on a limited budget so use of contractors restricted accordingly. When doing a background check the agent had to go to the location, find people who knew the subject, schedule interviews, write reports and sent them back to the case manager. Some reports resulted in additional checks.

Once the case manager had responses back from the various field investigators, the manager wrote a summary of finding, made a recommendation and send forward for approval. Urgent Security Checks could (and did) cut into the line and slow down processing the normal / routine requests.
